canonical.title: Eat Singapore: A First-Visit Food Guide for a Ghent Couple

siblings.title: Sleep — Singapore: Character Stays for a First Visit
siblings.summary: Character over category: shophouse, design, heritage and treehouse stays across Singapore's six base neighbourhoods, plus the one first-visit icon — with EUR/night bands and angle tags.

siblings.title: Do — Singapore: semi-adventurous activities for a first visit
siblings.summary: Trek-light, kayak, cycle, swim and snorkel-light dos around Singapore — difficulty, guide-need and half/full-day for each, plus activity-led day-trips.

siblings.title: See — Singapore: the unmissable icons + heritage to see (first-visit guide)
siblings.summary: The can't-miss Singapore icons, ethnic-quarter heritage, UNESCO Botanic Gardens, and offbeat sights — ranked must-do vs skippable, with EUR prices and booking lead times.

siblings.title: Offbeat Singapore: The Weird Stuff a First-Timer Misses
siblings.summary: A themed field guide to Singapore's strangest corners — hells, ghost reservoirs, last villages, leaning mosques and dragon kilns — far from the obvious icons.

siblings.title: Culture in Singapore: a first-visit guide to museums, festivals & crafts
siblings.summary: What cultural sights, festivals and workshops to plan a first Singapore trip around — marquee and offbeat, tagged by location and dated for 2026.

siblings.title: Around & day-trips — Singapore (first-visit guide)
siblings.summary: Changi-to-city options, getting around by MRT/Grab, and the day-trip orbit (Pulau Ubin, southern islands, Johor Bahru, Bintan) with times and EUR prices.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/best-chicken-rice-singapore/
sources.claim: Tian Tian at Maxwell tops local chicken-rice rankings; Anthony Bourdain praised it.

sources.title: https://www.timeout.com/singapore/restaurants/best-chilli-crab-singapore
sources.claim: Jumbo Seafood is the reliable benchmark chilli crab with multiple outlets.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/best-laksa-singapore-ranked/
sources.claim: 328 Katong Laksa is the iconic Katong laksa; noodles cut short to eat with a spoon.

sources.title: https://www.laupasat.sg/sataystreet/
sources.claim: Satay Street at Lau Pa Sat: nine open-air carts on Boon Tat Street nightly from 7pm.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/sg/en/article/features/singaporean-breakfast-kopitiam-kaya-toast-eggs
sources.claim: Classic Singaporean breakfast is kaya toast, soft eggs with soy and pepper, and kopi.

sources.title: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hill_Street_Tai_Hwa_Pork_Noodle
sources.claim: Hill Street Tai Hwa is Singapore's only Michelin-starred hawker stall, starred since 2016.

sources.title: https://www.nhb.gov.sg/what-we-do/our-work/sector-development/unesco/hawker-culture-in-singapore
sources.claim: Hawker centres are community dining rooms; hawker culture is a recognised heritage.

sources.title: https://ich.unesco.org/en/Decisions/15.COM/8.b.6
sources.claim: Singapore hawker culture inscribed on UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2020.

sources.title: https://www.nationalgeographic.com/travel/article/why-unesco-is-honoring-singapore-street-food
sources.claim: Singapore street food earned UNESCO recognition as a cultural treasure.

sources.title: https://www.visitsingapore.com/things-to-do/dining/local-food-and-drinks/order-coffee-like-a-local/
sources.claim: Official guide to ordering kopi using local Hokkien-Malay lingo.

sources.title: https://kopi.guide/
sources.claim: Kopi lingo: Kopi-C is evaporated milk + sugar; siew dai means less sweet.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/en/best-of/the-best-hawker-centers-in-singapore-and-what-to-order
sources.claim: Michelin's guide to the best hawker centres and what to order; chope-your-seat custom.

sources.title: https://singaporehawkercentres.com/best-stalls-maxwell-food-centre/
sources.claim: Maxwell's top stalls include Tian Tian, Ah Tai chicken rice and Fuzhou oyster cake.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/maxwell-food-centre-guide/
sources.claim: Ah Tai was founded by a former Tian Tian chef; its queue is usually shorter.

sources.title: https://singaporehawkercentres.com/best-stalls-chinatown-complex-food-centre/
sources.claim: Chinatown Complex is the largest centre with 200+ stalls; home to Hawker Chan; go off-peak.

sources.title: https://singaporehawkercentres.com/best-stalls-old-airport-road-food-centre/
sources.claim: Old Airport Road draws crowds for Nam Sing Hokkien mee, Lao Fu Zi CKT and Roast Paradise.

sources.title: https://danielfooddiary.com/2024/04/28/oldairportroadfoodcentre/
sources.claim: Old Airport Road Food Centre guide to its noodle and roast-meat stalls.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/tiong-bahru-market/
sources.claim: Tiong Bahru Market: Jian Bo chwee kueh (since 1958), famous CKT and dragon-fruit cheong fun.

sources.title: https://thehoneycombers.com/singapore/tiong-bahru-market-singapore/
sources.claim: Tiong Bahru Market has Bib Gourmand stalls: Hong Heng Hokkien mee, Tiong Bahru chicken rice.

sources.title: https://thehoneycombers.com/singapore/tekka-hawker-centre-food/
sources.claim: Tekka Centre in Little India is biryani central, with Allauddin's Michelin-recognised.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/tekka-centre/
sources.claim: Tekka serves Indian, Malay and Chinese street food; biryani, murtabak and prata at S$4-10.

sources.title: https://www.misstamchiak.com/newton-food-centre-singapore/
sources.claim: Newton Food Centre was a Crazy Rich Asians filming location with close to 100 stalls.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/newton-food-centre/
sources.claim: Newton is known for BBQ seafood and oyster omelette; prices run higher than other centres.

sources.title: https://islifearecipe.net/top-7-hawker-stalls-east-coast-lagoon-food-village/
sources.claim: East Coast Lagoon is a beloved seaside hawker centre; many stalls are cash-only.

sources.title: https://hungrygowhere.com/what-to-eat/east-coast-lagoon-food-village/
sources.claim: East Coast Lagoon is Singapore's only seaside hawker centre; sambal stingray and BBQ seafood.

sources.title: https://www.laupasat.sg/
sources.claim: Lau Pa Sat is a historic hawker centre and national monument near Raffles Place.

sources.title: https://taihwa.com.sg/
sources.claim: Hill Street Tai Hwa Pork Noodle official site for the Michelin-starred bak chor mee.

sources.title: https://sethlui.com/michelin-bak-chor-mee-showdown-singapore/
sources.claim: High Street Tai Wah is the sibling-rival serving a near-identical bowl without the queue.

sources.title: https://guide.michelin.com/en/best-of/where-to-find-the-best-chicken-rice-in-singapore
sources.claim: Michelin's guide to the best Hainanese chicken rice in Singapore.

sources.title: https://tiffycooks.com/chicken-rice-in-singapore-locals-actually-recommend/
sources.claim: Wee Nam Kee and hotel-tier Chatterbox are local chicken-rice recommendations.

sources.title: https://www.jumboseafood.com.sg/en/home
sources.claim: Jumbo Seafood official site; outlets at Riverside, Dempsey, ION and Jewel.

sources.title: https://hungrygowhere.com/what-to-eat/best-chilli-crab-singapore/
sources.claim: Chin Huat (Sri Lankan mud crab) and Mellben are top chilli-crab picks; JB Ah Meng for pepper crab.

sources.title: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilli_crab
sources.claim: Chilli crab is Singapore's national seafood dish.

sources.title: https://www.nlb.gov.sg/main/article-detail?cmsuuid=9bb609ca-dcf9-49eb-9941-86ff4ec2b2c5
sources.claim: Hooi Kok Wah refined chilli crab into the egg-thickened sambal version at Dragon-Phoenix, 1963.

sources.title: https://mothership.sg/2023/02/singapore-chilli-crab-creator-dies/
sources.claim: Chilli crab was invented by Cher Yam Tian in the mid-1950s.

sources.title: https://neighbourhoodlife.com.sg/best-laksa-singapore/
sources.claim: Janggut Laksa (1950s) claims to be the original Katong laksa creator.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/best-char-kway-teow-singapore-ranked/
sources.claim: Outram Park Fried Kway Teow Mee (Hong Lim, Bib Gourmand) is the wok-hei benchmark.

sources.title: https://sethlui.com/best-char-kway-teows-singapore/
sources.claim: No. 18 Zion Road and the 40-year Hill Street CKT are crispy-pork-lard favourites.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/best-hokkien-mee-singapore/
sources.claim: Swee Guan (Geylang Lor 29) cooks Hokkien mee over charcoal; Nam Sing and Hong Heng are Bib Gourmand.

sources.title: https://thebestofsingapore.com/singapore-best-hokkien-mee/
sources.claim: Guide to Singapore's best fried Hokkien mee stalls.

sources.title: https://www.monsterdaytours.com/post/10-best-fish-head-curry-in-singapore
sources.claim: Muthu's Curry and Banana Leaf Apolo are Little India's fish-head-curry institutions.

sources.title: https://www.misstamchiak.com/curry-fish-head/
sources.claim: Fish head curry combines Indian roots and Chinese love of fish head.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/best-prata-in-singapore/
sources.claim: Sin Ming Roti Prata is the all-rounder with great mutton curry.

sources.title: https://danielfooddiary.com/2021/11/04/pratasg/
sources.claim: Mr & Mrs Mohgan's prata is a cult favourite that often sells out by noon.

sources.title: https://hungrygowhere.com/what-to-eat/satay-singapore/
sources.claim: Haron Satay (East Coast Lagoon) and Chuan Kee Hainanese pork satay are top picks.

sources.title: https://sethlui.com/kwong-satay-singapore/
sources.claim: Kwong Satay in Geylang is known for charred caramelised pork-belly satay.

sources.title: https://www.timeout.com/singapore/restaurants/best-peranakan-restaurants-in-singapore
sources.claim: Guide to the best Peranakan restaurants and private dining in Singapore.

sources.title: https://www.comodempsey.sg/restaurant/candlenut
sources.claim: Candlenut is the world's first one-Michelin-star Peranakan restaurant, by chef Malcolm Lee.

sources.title: https://nag.sg/
sources.claim: Nyonyas & Gentlemen (Katong) runs a halal Peranakan lunch buffet.

sources.title: https://donsignaturecrab.sg/articles/food-guide-joo-chiat-katong/
sources.claim: Katong/Joo Chiat is the east-side Peranakan heart; Guan Hoe Soon is one of the oldest, plus nonya kueh.

sources.title: https://thehoneycombers.com/singapore/malay-food-singapore/
sources.claim: Hjh Maimunah (Bib Gourmand) and Warong Nasi Pariaman (1948) are top nasi padang spots.

sources.title: https://www.gedungkuning.sg/post/where-to-eat-in-kampong-glam-a-complete-food-guide
sources.claim: Kampong Glam food guide; Permata serves a Nusantara halal buffet in Gedung Kuning.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/nasi-lemak-in-singapore/
sources.claim: Selera Rasa (Adam Road) and The Coconut Club are top nasi lemak picks.

sources.title: https://sethlui.com/super-shiok-nasi-lemak-singapore/
sources.claim: Super Shiok Nasi Lemak (Bendemeer) carries a 4.9-star rating from 435 reviews.

sources.title: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Michelin-starred_restaurants_in_Singapore
sources.claim: Odette holds three Michelin stars (since 2019) for modern French cuisine.

sources.title: https://thehoneycombers.com/singapore/michelin-starred-restaurants-singapore/
sources.claim: Burnt Ends holds one Michelin star for wood-fired cooking by chef Dave Pynt.

sources.title: https://www.misslobang.com/article/best-kaya-toast-kopi-singapore-2026
sources.claim: Killiney (est. 1919) is the oldest kopitiam; Heap Seng Leong serves kopi gu you (butter coffee).

sources.title: https://neighbourhoodlife.com.sg/singapores-top-desserts-traditional-kueh-modern-creations/
sources.claim: Chendol and ice kachang are the classic cold hawker desserts.

sources.title: https://donsignaturecrab.sg/articles/best-durian-stalls-singapore-mao-shan-wang/
sources.claim: Mao Shan Wang is the prized durian; Geylang and Combat Durian are go-to stalls.

sources.title: https://www.timeout.com/singapore/things-to-do/your-ultimate-guide-to-durian-in-singapore
sources.claim: Durian peaks Jun-Aug and is banned on the MRT for its smell.

sources.title: https://ieatishootipost.sg/the-ultimate-singapore-durian-guide/
sources.claim: 99 Old Trees offers a durian 'omakase' experience; Geylang is the durian district.

sources.title: https://eatdrinktravel.com/best-cooking-class-singapore/
sources.claim: Food Playground (local-run) and Cookery Magic (Ruqxana, 21+ yrs) are standout cooking classes.

sources.title: https://eatdrinktravel.com/best-food-experiences-in-singapore/
sources.claim: Half-day food walks cover Kampong Glam, Little India and Chinatown.

sources.title: https://www.sassymamasg.com/eat-supper-spots-singapore-24-hour-late-night-food/
sources.claim: Chomp Chomp and Chong Pang Nasi Lemak (5pm-6:30am) are late-night supper spots.

sources.title: https://singaporehawkercentres.com/night-hawker-centre-in-singapore/
sources.claim: Makansutra Gluttons Bay (Marina Bay, from 5pm) is a scenic evening supper club.

sources.title: https://sethlui.com/best-oyster-omelette-orh-luak-singapore/
sources.claim: Lim's Fried Oyster (Berseh) is a must-visit for orh luak.

sources.title: https://www.misstamchiak.com/fried-oyster-omelette-singapore/
sources.claim: Hougang Oyster Omelette has 34+ years of history and a 4.3-star rating.

sources.title: https://songfa.com.sg/
sources.claim: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh is a Bib Gourmand Teochew pork-rib soup chain established 1969.

sources.title: https://eatbook.sg/song-fa-bak-kut-teh/
sources.claim: Song Fa is the first place many think of for peppery bak kut teh and held Bib Gourmand 8 years.

sources.title: https://www.sassymamasg.com/eat-peranakan-food-restaurants-singapore/
sources.claim: Baba Chews (former Katong police station) serves Peranakan classics and kueh.

sources.title: https://thehoneycombers.com/singapore/tiong-bahru-neighbourhood-guide/
sources.claim: Tiong Bahru is the walkable Art-Deco neighbourhood for cafes and brunch.

sources.title: https://tiongbahrubakery.com/
sources.claim: Tiong Bahru Bakery is the French bakery known for kouign-amann and pastries.
